text:
maria: Heads up — during the canary this morning ~12% we saw a subset of sessions persistently routed to the old variant even after cookie refreshes. Spotted from prod logs around 09:12 UTC. :eyes:

alex: Which split key are you using for this canary? cookie, header, or hash?

maria: It's a header-based split (X-Client-ID) with a sticky fallback to session cookie. Config snippet: `traffic.split: { by: header, header: "X-Client-ID", sticky: true }`

sam: Hmm. I briefly looked — we have header normalization happening in the edge proxy but the hash for split is calculated earlier in the request pipeline. If the proxy lowercases headers after sticky assignment we might be computing the hash on the original-case header, then later normalizing to lowercase for routing decisions, which leads to mismatch.

alex: That would explain why reloading the page (which refreshes the cookie) sometimes flips users but not consistently. Any logs showing header case?

maria: Pulled a few raw requests: `X-Client-ID: AbC123` vs `x-client-id: AbC123` across different gateways. Also saw cookies `redwood_sticky` present but pointing at old variant id.

jeff: ops-bot just rolled canary from 12% -> 20% at 09:05 UTC, might have exposed the timing window. ops-bot: `canary-rollout user: ops-bot percent: 20`

sam: Repro steps I'm trying locally: 1) craft request with mixed-case header; 2) force pipeline to compute hash pre-normalize; 3) set sticky cookie; 4) subsequent requests normalized -> routing uses post-normalize header but cookie points to old shard -> sticky overrides.

maria: Minimal curl repro I used: `curl -H "X-Client-ID: AbC123" -b "" -c cookies.txt https://api.redwood.dev/generate` then `curl -H "x-client-id: AbC123" -b cookies.txt https://api.redwood.dev/generate` — first assigns variant A, second still hits A but sometimes goes to B depending on edge instance.

alex: Quick mitigation idea: enforce header normalization as the very first middleware before hashing/sticky logic. That should make header-based buckets deterministic. Also add a short-term telemetry spike alert when header-case switching detected.

sam: Agreed. I'll prototype a tiny change to the routing middleware to `.toLowerCase()` header keys before computing the split hash. Also add a canary guard to block sticky writes if header normalization flag is not present.

jeff: Can we add a rollout guard rule to temporarily disable sticky cookies for header-based splits until the fix is live? Might reduce regression surface.

maria: Yes please — disable sticky for this specific canary id `canary-2026-03-20-09` until patch. I'll open a console rollback if we see >=1.5% error or 3xx/5xx spikes.

alex: I'll add telemetry: a counter for "header_case_mismatch" when we observe a request where the hashing-input header differs in case from the canonical header seen by the proxy. Throw an alert at 100 events/min.

sam: Plan: (1) small change to normalize headers pre-hash (PR), (2) disable sticky for canary `canary-2026-03-20-09` (console), (3) deploy and monitor telemetry for 30m, (4) re-enable sticky once stable. I'll draft PR and ping for review.

maria: Thanks. If anyone sees odd routing meanwhile ping me directly. :thumbsup:
